definitions.meaning: A well, spring, fountain (lit. and fig. )

quotations.old_english: Wæs ðēr wælla (fons) . . . ðe Hælend sæt ofer ðæm wælh
Tō ðē ðam willan ealles wīsdðmes
Heo ȝeoten i þan welle (wille, 2nd MS. ) ; þa wes þa welle mid attre bigon.

source_text: willa, wella, wylla, an. ; m. A well, spring, fountain (lit. and fig. ) :-- Wæs &d-bar;&e-long;r wælla (fons) . . . &d-bar;e Hæ-long;lend sæt ofer &d-bar;æm wælh, Jn. Skt. Rush. 4, 6, 14. In &d-bar;æm wælla, 9, 7. T&o-long; &d-bar;&e-long; &d-bar;am willan ealles w&i-long;sd&d-bar;mes ad te fontent omnis sapientiae, Bd. 5, 24 ; S. 649, 3. Mid &d-bar;am willan fulluhte bæþes fonte baptismatis, 5, 7; S. 620, 33. Ðiosne pytt &l-bar; uælla puteum, Jn. Skt. Lind. Rush. 4, 12. [Heo &yogh;eoten i þan welle (wille, 2nd MS. ) ; þa wes þa welle mid attre bigon. Laym. 19771.] v. wille, will.
